ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism), as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019, Executive Decrees No. 363 and 364 of 2015, and the Beneficial Ownership Registry regulations issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama; applicable to corporate virtual card issuers under the supervisory framework of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá and Panama’s AML/CFT authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or financial institution of the applicant

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and counterparties against the Panamanian Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) lists, OFAC SDN, US non-SDN sanctions, UN Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and PEP databases under Law 23/2015 as amended; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and politically exposed persons.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Online Name Reservation and Registration Portal (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa/portal-web/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script; Spanish may be required for legal designations; non-Spanish names must be transliterated into Latin characters; corporate suffix 'Sociedad Anónima' or abbreviations 'S.A.', 'Corp.', or 'Inc.' must be stated. Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic, or other non-Latin script is not accepted in the registered corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal ('recurso de apelación') with the Director General of the Registro Público within five business days of notification; if denied, the applicant may file an administrative claim ('demanda contencioso-administrativa') before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Panama or re-apply with a different name. A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days prior to expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole basis for a licensed B2B virtual card issuer; the issuer must maintain a physical office in Panama, local AML/CFT compliance staff, and adequate corporate substance. A virtual office may only be used as a supplementary communication address and will not satisfy the licensing test of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 75–90% probability of unannounced on-site inspections by Panamanian banking, AML, and financial supervisory authorities within the first 12 months after issuance of the card-issuing license; on-site inspection is a standard condition of this high-risk special license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas, Ley No. 32 de 1927, as amended, Articles 1–73; supplementary provisions of the Código de Comercio
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil, with protocolization before a Notario Público de la República de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation / Pacto Social y Estatutos) and certified testimonio filed for mercantile registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; registered capital may be nominal and fully subscribed, with no escrow or deposit obligation during incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: The subscriptions to the share capital stated in the public deed of incorporation are ratified and accepted in full. RESOLVED SECOND: The registered office is established at [Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the Registered Agent is appointed for service of process. RESOLVED THIRD: The following persons are appointed as officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until successors are duly elected. RESOLVED FOURTH: The President and Secretary are authorized, jointly and severally, to execute all documents and filings necessary to perfect the Company’s corporate existence and obtain all required licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Legal Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Reservas de Nombre / Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed corporate names through the Registro Público online reservation portal or by notarized petition. Verify absence of identical or confusingly similar existing registrations and obtain the official name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
Copy of incorporator identification or passport
Power of attorney if filed by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is queried, select an alternate name or submit an administrative reconsideration within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the S.A. charter including corporate purpose covering virtual card issuance and payment services. The subscribers must execute the Pacto Social y Estatutos before the notary, who verifies identity, capacity, and signature authenticity.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate name reservation certificate
Draft Pacto Social y Estatutos
Identification or passport of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct formal defects through a notarial amendment or addendum before protocolization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Protocolization and Issuance of Notarial Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary converts the executed charter into an Escritura Pública and issues a certified first testimonio. Confirm that the deed includes articles, registered agent, capital structure, and corporate governance provisions.
required_dossiers: Executed company charter
Notarial fee payment receipt
Certified copies of subscriber identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-protocolize with corrected instruments and obtain a fresh testimonio; no new registry hearing is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first testimonio of the Escritura Pública at the Mercantile Section. The Registry examines legality, assigns the corporate folio, and enters the Sociedad Anónima into the mercantile register. Obtain the certified corporate registration certificate.
required_dossiers: First testimonio of the Escritura Pública
Standard mercantile registration cover sheet
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a correction notice or Vista Fiscal, submit the amended deed or a supplementary clarification within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); Municipio de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) at DGI and file the Aviso de Operación with MICI and the corresponding municipal office. Register the company as an employer with CSS if hiring personnel.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate issued by the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Escritura Pública and statutes
Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
DGI RUC application form
MICI Aviso de Operación application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or MICI queries the application, submit missing proof of address, legalized corporate documents, or RUC clarification within fifteen calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Records and Registered Agent Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Resident Agent Licensed by the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate minute book, share ledger, officer election record, and written consents. Record the First Board Resolution and appoint the permanent resident agent required by Law 32 de 1927; file the agent acceptance and records with the Registry.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution and officer consent forms
Director and officer identification documents
Registered Agent service agreement
Share register and corporate minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify governance records and resubmit to the Registry; late filing surcharges, if imposed, are payable promptly to avoid loss of good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) for payment and virtual card issuance authorization
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Commercial Operating Notice) and, separately, SBP Authorization as Virtual Card Issuer / Payment Service Provider

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Registration (Registro de Impacto Ambiental) for office and managed data-center premises; no full Environmental Impact Study required for non-industrial fintech operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or regulated VOC emissions from card-issuance office operations; domestic sewage connected to licensed municipal sanitation; electronic waste and data hardware disposed through authorized recyclers; environmental compliance conditioned on zero unpermitted discharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety inspection and certification; structural load review certified by a registered engineer for server rooms and electrical installations; sanitary and workplace clearance issued by Ministerio de Salud (MINSA).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Functional portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sedeelectronica.dgi.gob.pa) for RUC (TIN) applications, e-filing of ISR and ITBMS, e-invoicing, and tax certificates; auxiliary platforms: DGI e-Tax, the electronic invoicing portal, call center and regional tax offices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Panamanian S.A.: 1) Appoint a resident attorney and a registered agent with a physical office in Panama (mandatory). 2) Submit the RUC pre-registration via the DGI Sede Electrónica or through the National Single Window for Investment (VUI), attaching: (a) certified copy of the Public Deed of Incorporation and by-laws; (b) apostilled/legalized incorporation certificates of any foreign parent entity, with Spanish translation; (c) notarized power of attorney in favor of the local agent; (d) final beneficial-owner sworn declaration (for CRS and economic substance); (e) valid identification documents of directors, officers and shareholders; (f) proof of the registered office address; and (g) the Aviso de Operación (commencement notice). 3) DGI issues the 20-digit RUC, simultaneously activating the ITBMS registration and municipal business license registration; the procedure is completed upon downloading the digital Registro Único de Contribuyentes certificate. 4) Activate the DGI e-Tax credentials and mandatory electronic invoicing account; complete the process within approximately 5–10 business days. There is no minimum capital requirement and no statutory share-capital deposit.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope — the Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) is a separately taxed legal person; no pass-through or transparent treatment exists. The S.A. pays corporate income tax (standard rate 25%; reduced statutory rates apply to qualifying SEM/CEP export-service income and specific licensed financial activities) only on Panamanian-source income and on profits derived from assets used or rights economically exercised in Panama. Foreign-source income (including fees from virtual card issuing, processing and spend-management services for non-resident merchants and foreign issuing banks) falls outside the Panamanian tax net where the service is performed and the economic use occurs abroad. Dividends distributed to shareholders are subject to a final 10% withholding tax at the corporate level; an alternative 4% minimum tax on undistributed taxable profits operates as a mechanism in lieu of actual distribution. A zero-tax status is available only within statutorily recognized tax-exempt zones (e.g., Colón Free Zone, SEM/CEM regional headquarters, Ciudad del Saber).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections exist under Panamanian law; classification follows the Código Fiscal and DGI rulings. Available elections: (i) Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente (RPC) — optional for gross annual income up to B/. 36,000, substituting ISR and ITBMS filings with a fixed monthly quota (B/. 50–B/. 300); (ii) SEM/CEM Multinational Headquarters Regime (Law 41 of 2007, Law 21 of 2017) — election for a 5% income tax rate on qualifying export services, 0% ITBMS on intra-group services and full foreign-source characterization; (iii) Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) and written advance tax rulings on transfer-pricing treatments for cross-border card-network flows; (iv) the Innovative Enterprises (fintech) licensing regime under Law 242 of 2021, under which qualified digital-payment companies may obtain special administrative and fiscal treatment through an advance DGI ruling.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panama's VAT-type national consumption tax governed by Código Fiscal Title III and administered by DGI. Standard rate 7%; alcohol and tobacco products 10%; gambling services 15%. Pure interest and financial spreads are generally exempt, while card-issuing, acquiring, processing and spend-management fees are taxable at the standard rate unless zero-rated as exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis registration threshold: every person carrying out taxable transfers or services in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable event, regardless of turnover. A statutory simplified regime threshold applies for small taxpayers: annual gross income up to B/. 36,000 (Balboa, pegged 1:1 to the US dollar) can elect the fixed-monthly-quota RPC instead of the standard ITBMS/ISR filing. A special simplified ITBMS registration regime is also applicable to non-domiciled digital-service providers supplying services to Panamanian consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (eFactura) applies to all ITBMS-registered taxpayers under the DGI electronic-invoicing technical standard introduced by DGI Resolution and phased in since 2020. Issuers must use DGI-authorized software or the free DGI portal; each invoice is filed to the DGI for near-real-time validation and receives a unique digital authorization code (digital stamp) before or at the moment of issuance. The system requires XML-format invoicing, digital signatures, and periodic reporting (daily, weekly or quarterly depending on taxpayer category). The DGI automatically cross-reconciles the e-invoicing database with ITBMS returns, customs records, banking information and card-settlement data, effectively operating as a centralized fiscal clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% ITBMS applies where tangible goods are physically exported from Panamanian customs territory, the Customs Export Declaration is issued in the exporter's name, and the commercial invoice is addressed to a non-resident purchaser. Services: 0% applies where (i) the service is performed and the benefit is enjoyed wholly outside Panama, (ii) the service is directly related to exported goods, or (iii) the recipient is a qualifying SEM/CEM regional-headquarters company. For a corporate virtual-card issuer, network, processing, interchange and spend-management fees invoiced to foreign merchants, foreign issuing banks and non-resident cardholders qualify as zero-rated export services when the processing location, merchant establishment, card account or bank is outside Panama and no Panamanian fixed establishment economically consumes the service. Claimants must hold a written contract evidencing the non-resident beneficiary, demonstrate commercial-economic substance, maintain transfer-pricing documentation at arm's length, and show foreign-currency collection normally within 180 days of invoice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Mercancías) with exit authorization and customs seal
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing despatch to a non-resident consignee
Commercial invoice with RUC, Incoterms, full description, quantity and value
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT / Foreign Currency Receipt Voucher evidencing the foreign-currency payment credited to the exporter's account

Supporting service-export proof: signed contract or service order, card-network settlement statements (Mastercard/Visa Direct records), and certification of non-resident use or consumption for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI automatically cross-matches zero-rated ITBMS declarations with customs cargo manifests, banking records and card-network settlement data; discrepancies generate immediate audit flags. Sanctions: (i) restitution of the unpaid 7% ITBMS plus statutory overdue interest and late-payment surcharges (generally 10%–50% depending on delay); (ii) administrative fines from B/. 1,000 to B/. 100,000 against the taxpayer and its legal representative; (iii) publication of the penalty and disqualification from future export-refund claims; (iv) criminal tax-fraud prosecution under Código Penal Articles 310–313 with imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and disqualification from public contracts. The DGI may reopen the last 5 fiscal years (or 10 years where no return was filed) and claw back previously granted refunds with interest; the registered agent and shareholders may incur joint and several liability for gross negligence in the filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama has no traditional central bank. The U.S. dollar is unrestricted legal tender, and Banco Nacional de Panamá operates as a state-owned commercial bank rather than a monetary authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized and freely convertible monetary system. Both current-account and capital-account transactions may be settled without exchange-control approval. Profit, dividend, and capital remittances are unrestricted; only normal AML/CFT documentary due diligence applies to outbound and inbound USD transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply to export receipts. Exporters may retain proceeds in USD either abroad or in Panamanian local banks. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender or repatriation duty, although banks may request supporting export documents under AML/CFT procedures.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Concentrator operational account / treasury clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium. An offshore digital EMI without a Panamanian license cannot directly access local USD clearing or ACH Panama except through a licensed sponsor bank. International EMIs may onboard the Panamanian S.A. as a corporate client, but local merchant payouts require a sponsor relationship with an SBP-licensed bank or a locally licensed payment service provider. Foreign EMI passporting is not recognized; a local payment institution or sponsored banking agent is the legally prudent route.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical board presence is not absolutely mandated by statute; apostilled corporate documents and a properly notarized power of attorney are legally recognized. In practice, SBP-licensed tier-1 banks require either in-person attendance by at least one director/authorized signer or a live video interview. Remote account opening is rarely granted during the first relationship, and a local registered agent/compliance officer significantly improves onboarding success.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: B2B virtual card issuing is classified as a high-risk payment/processor-type activity, triggering bank de-risking and heightened correspondent banking scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the company's SBP license or license-application evidence, full AML/CFT policy manual, independent compliance audit, designated compliance officer, transaction-monitoring system description, flowcharts of card loads and disbursements, card scheme sponsorship agreement, and a detailed expected-transaction profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Panama S.A. structures with historical bearer shares, nominee directors, or layered foundations raise UBO tracing concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit notarized incorporation deed, current and complete registered share register proving cancellation of any bearer instruments, written beneficial ownership declarations, official ID/passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation, notarized board resolutions, and a clear economic-substance explanation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual card loads from unexplained third-party funding or cryptocurrency-linked sources are treated as money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a source-of-funds policy, bank reference letters, load-source whitelist, proof of participant KYC and CDD, corresponding bank statements, merchant-category-code screening rules, transaction monitoring audit trails, and a documented procedure for rejecting unverifiable funding sources.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections must be routed over SWIFT MT103 to the S.A.'s named bank account, with the company RUC, originator/beneficiary details, and a clear purpose code such as 'equity capital / share subscription / paid-in capital contribution.' The supporting subscription agreement, capital-increase resolution, and UBO details are retained in the bank compliance file. Since Panama clears in USD, no FX conversion or central-bank approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and merchant disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments, MT202 for interbank treasury transfers, and ACH Panama for low-value local USD settlement. Commercial letters of credit are issued through SBP-licensed banks using SWIFT MT700 where payee-side assurance is needed. Mastercard/Visa network rails remain the dedicated clearing path for virtual-card transactions, settling in USD via the sponsor bank's card settlement accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-applicable for the USD functional balance sheet: the Panamanian balboa is pegged at 1:1 and USD is legal tender, so no converting hedge is required.

FX forwards and NDFs are permissible when non-USD operational currencies such as COP, MXN, or BRL create invoice exposure; such contracts may be booked through SBP-licensed banks or investment-grade counterparties.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible for material non-USD operating cash flows, provided the counterparty is an authorized bank or recognized financial institution and the transaction is evidenced by an ISDA agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única / Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each incorporation anniversary (anniversary-date rule; e.g., an S.A. incorporated on 15 April must pay on or before 14 July each year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic statutory recargo of 10% plus monthly default interest at 1%; the Public Registry blocks registration of share transfers, director appointments, amendments, and capital increases until the tax is settled; the entity loses paz y salvo status and cannot obtain good-standing certificates; prolonged multi-year arrears expose the corporation to the Public Registry's inactive-company purge program and eventual administrative strike-off. Fee tiered under Law 70 of 2019: US$300 (assets under US$1 million), US$600 (US$1-10 million), US$900 (over US$10 million).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta, Form 2) with attached audited financial statements if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year-end (within three months of year-end; taxpayers on an approved non-calendar fiscal year must file within three months of their approved year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% recargo plus 1% monthly interest on any tax due; administrative fines for failure to file or late filing under the Fiscal Code; the DGI may reconstruct income, assess tax ex officio, and pursue coercive collection; for licensed payment entities, delinquent declaration also constitutes a regulatory compliance breach.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Ownership Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each incorporation anniversary; any change in shareholding or control must be updated within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late or inaccurate filings (generally US$500-US$10,000); persistent non-confirmation is treated as an AML/CFT compliance deficiency, which the SBP may weigh against the card issuer's license renewal and the resident agent may not certify.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and annual report filed with the financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) - Supervised Money Services / Card Issuer License
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the 31 December fiscal year-end (30 April deadline), or earlier if required by the SBP license conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative offenses under the SBP licensing regime; fines, warnings, or suspension of the money-services authorization, and failure to file may invalidate the license's good standing for cross-border card network agreements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is compulsory when (i) gross revenues subject to Panamanian tax in the preceding year exceed US$1,500,000; (ii) the entity holds an SBP money-services or card-issuing license, which mandates annual audited IFRS financial statements regardless of size; or (iii) the DGI, a lender, or a shareholder agreement requires one. An inactive S.A. with no Panamanian-source operations and no license is generally not required to file audited financial statements with any authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as issued by the IASB is mandatory for SBP-regulated entities and is the framework accepted for the DGI-mandated audited financial statements; non-supervised corporations may apply Panamanian GAAP (PCGA), which is substantially IFRS-aligned; accounting records must be maintained in Spanish or be readily translatable for the DGI.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 129 of 2020, as re-established by the 2023 beneficial-ownership regime, every Panamanian juridical person must file and annually re-confirm its ultimate beneficial owners with the DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry within 30 days of each incorporation anniversary and within 30 days of any change. For the card-issuing S.A., any transfer of shares that alters the beneficial ownership or control structure requires (i) entry of the transfer in the corporation's stock ledger, (ii) filing of the UBO update with the DGI, and (iii) prior written no-objection from the SBP before the transfer of a controlling interest is consummated, per the money-services license conditions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registro de Acciones / Stock Ledger with share transfers and endorsements)
Register of Directors (director and officer appointments, resignations, and indemnification entries)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas for board and shareholder meetings)
Legal and AML/CFT files (client identity data and transaction records under Law 23 of 2015)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350 - US$1,200 per year for resident agent, registered office, and routine secretarial maintenance of a licensed Panamanian S.A.; turnover-based SBP annual supervision assessment applies in addition to the license fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000 - US$18,000 for a mid-size Panamanian operating S.A.; US$25,000 - US$75,000 for an SBP-supervised virtual card issuer requiring IFRS consolidated audited financial statements and regulatory reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general CIT holiday for card issuers. The territorial regime excludes foreign-source income from Panamanian tax. A licensed multinational headquarters under the SEM regime may obtain preferential treatment on qualifying cross-border group services, but Panama-source card issuance, interchange, and merchant processing fees remain taxable at 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1050 – Declaración de Renta Anual de Personas Jurídicas, filed electronically through the DGI Sede Electrónica (Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with mandatory prepayment or estimated-installment obligations during the fiscal year where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within three months after the close of the fiscal year; a calendar-year Sociedad Anónima must file no later than March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from Panamanian-source operations, including card scheme rebates, interchange fees, SaaS/issuing platform fees, and merchant spend-management fees, net of returns and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source income. Foreign-source income attributable to the multinational group is excluded unless it is effectively connected to a Panama permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable costs and expenses allocated to Panamanian-source income, including salaries, technology and payment-processing costs, network license fees, AML compliance costs, and bank charges, provided they are documented and arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported by invoices, settlement reports, and transfer pricing documentation. Related-party payments are accepted only if priced at arm's length and accompanied by contemporaneous economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory deductions, exempt territorial items, and the 5-year net operating loss carryforward, where substantiated.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any loss carryforward must be reconciled with prior-year filed returns. Foreign-source losses cannot offset Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed CIT liability at 25% of the net taxable base, after applying creditable taxes withheld at source and authorized prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot shelter Panama-source taxable profits through unreported distributions; all prepayments and credits must be traceable to Panama bank settlements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment trigger a fine of up to B/.5,000.00, a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax, and monthly interest at approximately 1% per month from the original due date. Continued non-filing permits DGI to make an official desk assessment and enforce seizure of bank accounts and payment-rail settlements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on gross dividends distributed to shareholders out of Panama-source taxable profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction, present it to the Panamanian S.A. before payment, and file with DGI the formal treaty-relief application. The S.A. must maintain the DGI approval, beneficial-ownership declaration, source-of-funds documentation, and computing records to justify the reduced withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties for use of intangibles in Panama is 10%; interest paid to non-resident lenders is generally subject to a 5% statutory withholding. Depending on the applicable Panama Double Tax Agreement, the rate may be reduced to 0-5% for interest and 0-10% for royalties, subject to bona fide beneficial ownership proof.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Panama taxpayer must prepare and file a Transfer Pricing Local File/informative return when annual gross revenue exceeds B/.3 million; a Master File is additionally required for multinational groups with consolidated group annual revenue above B/.100 million. Controlled cross-border transactions above B/.1 million require transaction-level functional and economic analysis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama ESR Law 254 of 2021 applies. A virtual card issuer engaged in financial services must perform core income-generating activities in Panama, maintain a licensed physical office and locally resident employees, keep books in Panama, hold board meetings in Panama, and demonstrate that card-issuance, risk, AML/KYC, network contract, and settlement decisions are managed from Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally under-reporting Panama-source interchange or fee revenue, inflating deductions, issuing false invoices from related shell companies, or booking card portfolio profits to foreign nominee banks to avoid CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to 100%-300% of the evaded tax, surcharges, monthly interest, criminal prosecution under Panama's Código Fiscal, and imprisonment of 3 to 6 years in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or direct the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, subject to civil restitution, travel bans, and conviction with imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A. as a pure mailbox entity with no physical office, no local payroll, no board records in Panama, and no ESR compliance while claiming treaty benefits or tax residency status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registered agent de-registration, loss of tax benefits, DGI recharacterization of all revenue, fines under Law 254 of 2021, and revocation of the corporate license and tax identification number.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panamanian courts will pierce the corporate veil. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners must personally restore diverted funds, face civil restitution, and may be subjected to travel bans and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing corporate virtual cards as issuer of record without the required SBP license, lacking a KYC/AML program, or processing transactions for sanctions targets, shell companies, or unexplained third-party beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP financial regulations ranging from B/.150,000 to B/.5 million per violation, mandatory closure, confiscation of settlement funds, and criminal referral for money-laundering offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may be individually fined, removed from the financial system, denied banking access, banned from travel, and imprisoned for money-laundering or terrorist-financing offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, management fees, data-processing fees, or card-network rebate allocations to a related offshore intermediary without economic substance, or failing to file the Local and Master File when the threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may re-price the controlled transactions, impose a 25% CIT adjustment, and levy penalties of up to 100% of the adjusted tax plus interest. Transfer-pricing documentation failures carry additional fixed monetary fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length intercompany terms are jointly liable for the additional assessment; deliberate profit-stripping can be prosecuted as criminal tax evasion and leads to director travel bans and imprisonment.
